questions.q: In the two-stage retrieval architecture, what is Stage 1's job and how many candidates does it retrieve?
options: Precisely score every document in the corpus and return the top 5
Compress the query and documents into one vector and compare distances corpus-wide
Cheaply retrieve 50–200 candidates for recall, leaving precise scoring to Stage 2
Run an LLM judge over the whole corpus and pick the best paragraphs
questions.explain: Stage 1 is the vector index retrieving 50–200 candidates cheaply for recall; Stage 2 (the reranker) scores only those candidates precisely for precision.

questions.q: Why does a cross-encoder rank query-document pairs more precisely than a bi-encoder?
options: It produces smaller vectors, so cosine distance is computed faster
It takes the query and one document together as input, so joint attention sees the actual words of both
It trains on more dimensions, so the embedding space has higher recall
It skips tokenization and compares raw character counts directly
questions.explain: A cross-encoder feeds the query and document together into one forward pass, letting it reward exact answer matches, penalize topic-only overlap, and understand negation — but it is too slow to run over a whole corpus.

questions.q: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) used for in the reranking pipeline?
options: Compressing two embedding models into one vector space
Merging the vector ranking and the full-text ranking from hybrid search without needing comparable scores
Fusing the query embedding with the document embedding before scoring
Retraining the cross-encoder on reciprocal document pairs
questions.explain: RRF combines rankings from multiple retrieval paths — the chapter's hybrid search produces a vector ranking and a full-text ranking that disagree, and RRF merges them rank-based without comparable scores.

questions.q: According to the chapter's latency budgets, how long does Cohere Rerank take for 50 documents, and what is the total two-stage retrieval budget?
options: 80–150ms for the rerank call; total two-stage retrieval stays under 300ms, well within a 500ms SLA
5–15ms for the rerank call; total retrieval must stay under 50ms
500–800ms for the rerank call; the SLA is 2 seconds for interactive search
1–2 seconds for the rerank call; it is normally the pipeline bottleneck
questions.explain: Fifty documents through Cohere Rerank typically completes in 80–150ms round-trip, and total two-stage retrieval stays under 300ms — well within a 500ms SLA for interactive search.

questions.q: In a SQL Server RAG pipeline, how should responsibilities be divided between the database and the reranker?
options: SQL Server does the final top-5 ordering and the cross-encoder only handles tenant filtering
Both run the same scoring; the reranker just doubles as a backup
The reranker retrieves the candidates and SQL Server re-orders them with T-SQL
SQL Server owns recall (tenant-filtered top-50 with a distance threshold); the reranker owns precision (final top-5 order)
questions.explain: The chapter draws a clean boundary: SQL Server owns recall with tenant filtering and a distance threshold, while the cross-encoder or Cohere Rerank owns the final top-5 ordering for precision.
